title: The ten days
hookLine: no days are dearer to Allah for good deeds than the first ten of Dhul Hijjah (Bukhari)

lines: A SEASON FOR THOSE AT HOME.
cards: Ramadan is usually the month that comes to mind first when the holiest days of the Islamic year come up, and its nights carry Laylat al-Qadr. But a hadith in Bukhari points somewhere else.
It names a different stretch of days, about two months after Ramadan ends, at the start of the last month of the year, the month of pilgrimage.
While pilgrims are heading for Mecca, everyone else, at home, is also in a season. Today: the ten days.

teach.h: NO DAYS DEARER FOR GOOD DEEDS.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn 'Abbas reports that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said there are no days in which good deeds are more beloved to God than these, meaning the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah. The companions were startled.
Not even striving in the path of God? Not even that, he said, except a man who goes out with his life and his wealth and comes back with nothing.
An ordinary good deed, done in these ten days, is set beside the hardest sacrifice there is. Commentators also connect the days to the Qur'an.

teach.h: BY THE DAWN, AND TEN NIGHTS.
teach.b: Surah Al-Fajr opens with an oath, by the dawn, and ten nights, and commentators going back to Ibn 'Abbas understood those ten nights as these.

And Surah Al-Hajj speaks of remembering God's name on appointed days, which Ibn 'Abbas is reported to have explained as the ten. What do people do? More of what they already do: extra prayer, charity, reading, kindness.
Some fast the first nine days.
Others fast at least the ninth, the day of 'Arafah, when the pilgrims stand on the plain; a hadith in Sahih Muslim hopes that fast wipes away the faults of the year before and the year after.
Some companions, Bukhari notes, used to walk through the markets in these days saying the takbir aloud, and people around them took it up.
And a hadith in Muslim says that someone planning to offer a sacrifice for Eid shouldn't cut their hair or nails from the start of the month, a small mark in the body that the season has begun.
The point isn't a new set of rules.

teach.h: THE SAME DEEDS, A HEAVIER SEASON.
teach.b: It's a window: the same deeds, in a season when they weigh more.

how: In the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah many Muslims increase prayer, charity, remembrance and takbir; many fast the day of 'Arafah, and some fast the first nine days.

games.why: they asked about striving in God's path. he said not even that, except one who goes out with life and wealth and returns with nothing.

practice: Think of ten days, starting today, and choose one small good you could add to each: a text to someone who's lonely, a coin in a box, ten minutes of reading, picking up litter on the walk home.
Picture doing it near the end, when you're tired; if it still fits, keep it. If you pray, you can make your intention now.

wordCard.voice: Dhul Hijjah. The month of pilgrimage, whose first ten days the hadith calls dearer to God for good deeds than any other days. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Dhul Hijjah, the month of the pilgrimage, the last month of the Hijri year.
